decision: user 2026-10-30: probe, then skip unreferenced zone zeros only if proven

probe_1_prefilled.disk: 200 GB dynamic VHDX hot-added to the lab VM (SCSI 0:7), removed and deleted afterwards
probe_1_prefilled.steps: raw-fill first 30 GB with random bytes (254 s); GPT; Dev Drive ReFS format (2.7 s); metadata-inclusive bitmap; count 4 KiB zero granules in the zone; 20 GB stress (665 big files, 5,000 small, 30% deleted); guest reboot; verify
probe_1_prefilled.finding: the format left 99.99% of the zone zero although it had held random data, in 2.7 s: a TRIM/unmap the dynamic VHDX honours, not 22 GB of zero writes. So on a thin device format does clear the zone and this run cannot show whether ReFS tolerates old data there; the direct test (randomize every zero granule after format) follows.
